contentBlocks.body: A parameter annotation tells TypeScript what kind of value a function expects.
Without an annotation, a parameter is implicitly any and strict mode reports an error. Annotating parameters is the first habit to build: it documents the function and lets every caller be checked.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which annotation describes a string parameter?

payload.explanation: TypeScript places the type after a colon.

payload.text: A parameter that is either true or false is annotated as isReview: ____.

knowledgeItems.prompt: In strict mode, what happens to an unannotated parameter such as function f(x) { }?

choices: It is implicitly any, which strict mode reports as an error
It is inferred from the function name
payload.answer: It is implicitly any, which strict mode reports as an error
payload.explanation: TypeScript cannot infer a parameter's type from nothing, so it falls back to any; noImplicitAny (part of strict) turns that into an error.
